approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. Its connected-fragment crossover and local edits include a retained formula-preserving exchange of aromatic nitrogen positions, and stable identity checks admit a surplus of novel candidates. A Gaussian process trained on the full accepted-score archive compares integer counts of local molecular environments using generalized Tanimoto covariance. For each batch slot, the Parent takes a separate correlated posterior draw and submits its best available molecule. Accepted feedback updates both the breeding population and the prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Choose each molecule for the additional predicted best score it brings to the batch. Pair the existing full posterior draws with their reflections around the unchanged predictive mean, then greedily cover high scores across this shared panel. A molecule that mostly repeats peaks already covered by earlier choices has little marginal value. The earlier batch-coordination sibling conditioned pending molecules to their predicted means and reduced sampling variance; this rule keeps that variation and compares marginal batch utility instead. Other siblings changed breeding, graph edits, identity admission or the predictive model. None of the supplied siblings has tested this expected-batch-maximum allocation rule. Its usefulness depends on actual evaluated outcomes, not on wider chemical coverage.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 completes all supplied evaluations with macro mean 0.574343936523512 and population SD 0.012316775530180069. Reading its actual three summary.json/run.log pairs and all task logs confirms 624 strict best-generating-parent beats and 241 incumbent improvements among 4350 accepted offspring. The targeted behavior is independent slot allocation: each full function draw contributes its masked maximizer, while earlier selections affect only identity exclusion. There is no marginal expected-batch-maximum calculation. A passive replay of all 435 logged pools proves that the final Parent set already covers every pool maximum of its original batch-sized sample panel; merely optimizing that same small panel would therefore be a vacuous claimed improvement. The proposed shared panel adds the mean-reflected counterpart of each logged draw without changing the predictive model or consuming randomness. On these fixed Parent inputs, the registered greedy rule with exact-zero-gain mean completion changes 433 batch sets and 3970 positions; 3154 of 3453 positive-marginal-gain later decisions differ from the Parent draw maximizer on the identical available mask. Its panel-average batch maximum increases in 378 pools and ties in 57, with mean difference 0.006756245488058684; these are sampled utility values, not oracle scores. There are 462 zero-gain completion slots. Mean nonempty Murcko-core coverage falls from 6.9816091954022985 to 6.866666666666666 and mean count-fingerprint similarity rises by 0.004418903163794924, so this is not evidence for a diversity mechanism. The prior sibling n-521f362b3777 activated mean-fantasy covariance contraction and changed 287 batch sets, but its paired macro delta was -0.0018442146149799665. That result and the older uncertainty-allocation observation n-fc2c108a5253 do not establish that lower covariance or changed choices improve scores. The Parent also retains undercovered latent intervals: its supplied count-posterior audit reports 76.9 percent nominal 95 percent coverage. The present hypothesis connects allocation to a batch-maximum objective while leaving that model limitation unresolved. Reproducible passive audit and all per-batch decisions are in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-07-improve-L01-improve.plan_audit.py, .plan_audit.json and .plan_audit.batches.jsonl; no optimizer search, smoke run or oracle call was performed.
hypothesis: Allocate the batch by greedy marginal expected-maximum gain over a shared antithetic panel of the inherited joint posterior draws, so each selection accounts for the score peaks already covered by earlier selections.

finding_summary.headline: Batch-maximum allocation changes choices but lowers mean final score by 0.0161
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes a real effect from later marginal allocation, beyond the first mean-ranked choice or antithetic arithmetic alone. It also shows that correctly increasing the model's sampled batch maximum is insufficient to improve the final best evaluated score on this panel. The original predictive model and random draws remain intact on identical inputs, narrowing the explanation to the changed allocation and its subsequent feedback trajectory. Unavailable alternative molecules have no oracle labels, so same-pool utility comparisons cannot identify which individual replacements caused the score losses.

The objective rewards a batch's maximum without requiring it to beat the incumbent, and twenty dependent antithetic scenarios approximate the model's tails. Together with the selected-stream uncertainty undercoverage, these leave a concrete mismatch between acquisition utility and useful search progress. More incumbent updates and lower selected-stream prediction error also failed to produce a higher endpoint: improvement frequency and average prediction accuracy do not measure how far the search advances. Because the later selected molecules differ, the MSE comparison does not establish better prediction or calibration on common molecules. An incumbent-relative utility or a separately tested correction to predictive uncertainty is worth distinguishing next; neither is established as the cause here. On the Child's fixed pools, mean count-fingerprint similarity falls from 0.6860 to 0.6810, yet distinct nonempty cores per batch also fall from 6.846 to 6.641 and acyclic selections rise from 104 to 145. Similarity instead increases when the same rule is applied to the Parent's pools. This separates lower pairwise similarity from broader core coverage and shows that the secondary effects depend on the pool.

The molecular assessment finds useful polar motifs within ring-rich families alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, constrained ring systems and unspecified stereochemistry. Smaller molecules do not consistently give better endpoints. Allocation preserves those chemical limitations, so the internal utility increase supplies no evidence of improved feasibility or broadly useful chemistry.
finding_summary.results:
The rule changes 431 of 435 submitted batch sets versus independent posterior draws on the same pools. All 3,596 later choices with positive marginal value follow the registered maximizer; 3,256 differ from the original draw's choice on the identical available mask. Another 319 positions use the registered mean completion after sampled gains reach exactly zero. Average maximum over the shared scenario panel rises by 0.00617, with 396 pools improving and 0 declining. This is internal sampled utility.

Evaluated three-seed mean final score falls from 0.57434 to 0.55824, a change of -0.01610 against the registered +0.002 target. Seed changes are −0.03008, +0.01124 and −0.02948; 8 of 15 task/seed endpoints decline, and every task's mean declines. The largest mean loss is sitagliptin at 0.05362. Strict improvements over the best generating parent are 621/4,350 versus 624/4,350, and incumbent improvements are 250 versus 241. Mean evaluated batch maximum falls from 0.48731 to 0.45721, while prediction MSE on each run's selected stream falls from 0.01127 to 0.00924. Nominal 95% latent intervals cover 77.86% of selected scores versus 76.92% for the Parent. All evaluations complete; no numerical fallback occurs.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families acquire useful polar motifs, but reactive bonds, strained-looking bridges and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: Node n-0db88abff519 produces recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments within heavily edited ring systems: indoles with cyano/enamine or amidine groups, acceptor-rich heteroaromatics, aryl-linked saturated amines, cyclic amides and fluorinated carbonyl/imino heterocycles. All five supplied tasks were read; the digest's tasks_without_trajectories list is empty. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Digest ring_closure_rate spans 0.9563 to 0.9782 and aromatic_atom_rate spans 0.954 to 0.9736; these are fractions of strings containing the indicated features, not fractions of atoms or measures of ring diversity. The chemistry has abundant rings and aromatic atoms, with multiple families across seeds but substantial congeneric concentration within them. Passive RDKit inspection of every supplied Child and Parent trajectory gives Child median heavy-atom counts of 25, 34, 30, 34 and 28 in the stated task order. Size changes relative to Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 are mixed, and smaller molecules do not uniformly accompany better recorded endpoints. Plausible motifs coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, thiols, unusual arene bridges, unsaturated small rings and oversized assemblies. All task stereocentre_rate values are 0.0, despite many apparent stereogenic centres. Charged_rate is 0.0 except 0.0011 in the final task; neutral SMILES do not imply an absence of protonatable amines. These are connectivity-based chemical judgments, not measured stability, synthesis, affinity or mechanism activation. Reproducible structural counts, exact observed seed endpoints, input hashes and digest-molecule descriptors are in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-07-improve-L01-molecular.audit.json, generated by the adjacent audit.py with the supplied RDKit 2023.09.6 environment. Counts in this report refer to trajectory occurrences, excluding initial molecules unless stated otherwise; ring-size checks use RDKit-perceived rings.

per_task.generated_character: The main products are compact, mostly aromatic indole/aniline relatives, with a median of 25 heavy atoms and digest mean SMILES length 40.9. The best molecule, at 0.4572645941803378, has 24 heavy atoms, an indole NH, a phenyl group, two methoxy substituents, a carbon-bonded nitrile and an exocyclic anilinoalkene. A thiol-substituted alkene analogue reaches 0.4455495560238204. Another leading family combines an N-hydroxy-N-aryl amidine with an unusually bridged aromatic system, reaching 0.4451945621839941. Late seed-2 molecules retain the aromatic/amidine framework but add N-F, N-Cl and halomethyl ethers. This is a real change in functional groups from the Parent: carbon-bonded nitriles occur in 105 Child proposals versus none in the Parent, while the passive amide flag falls from 705 to 46. Both streams retain the same median heavy-atom count. The straightforward substituted-indole connectivity is more synthetically recognizable than the short bridged or heteroatom-halogen variants; no route or stability evidence is supplied.
liabilities: The thiol-bearing alkene, N-hydroxyamidine and exocyclic enamine introduce potential reactivity or tautomeric uncertainty; their scores do not establish storage stability or a synthetic route.
Late N-F/N-Cl substitutions and halomethyl ethers raise chemical stability concerns without surpassing the best simpler indole. The bridged amidine structures also require geometric scrutiny.
Unassigned stereogenic features and unspecified alkene/imine geometry remain in the more elaborate families; the digest contains no stereochemical assignments.
missing_features: The compact aromatic framework and connected polar substituents seen in the leaders are missing from the fragment tail and incompletely preserved in ring-expanded late congeners.

The favorable carbon-bonded cyano/enamine arrangement is absent from the leading amidine family, while the best cyano molecule lacks that family's amidine. The visible scores support alternative heteroatom arrangements and do not identify a further mandatory heterocycle or functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Its higher-scoring descendants retain compact aromatic extent while changing the carbonyl-linked functionality to cyano/enamine, thiol-alkene or amidine arrangements. The Child's upper observed score quartile contains only 22-27 heavy atoms; the low tail includes water, ethene and FSSF at 0.0. Removing aromaticity from part of a late amidine framework accompanies a score of 0.09690882872436221. These observations favor a connected, compact aromatic scaffold with suitably placed heteroatoms, not indiscriminate ring addition. Several different bridged amidine connectivities share 0.4451945621839941, so the records do not establish a unique preferred topology. Parent and Child best values remain close in seeds 0 and 1, while seed 2 changes from 0.4484138510190879 to 0.4031937733859023; replacing amides with other nitrogen chemistry is not a uniform score improvement.

per_task.generated_character: This stream consists largely of densely substituted polyheteroaromatics. The best family has a fused aza/oxa carbonyl core joined through sulfur to a phenyl-pyridyl system. The leader has 34 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings, two carbon-bonded nitriles, an O-cyanate and a formate ester. Equally scoring congeners substitute thioformate, formate or acetate groups. Other seeds produce bulkier carbonyl-rich fused nitrogen heterocycles with aryl ethers, sulfur-containing chains and extensive halogenated substituents; the final seed-2 examples include 46-47 heavy atoms. Relative to the Parent, mean heavy-atom count falls from 51.13333333333333 to 36.89885057471265 and mean SMILES length from 94.56436781609196 to the digest's rounded 67.2. Nevertheless, 142 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms and the largest contains 113. Recognizable heteroaryl connections coexist with much less routine combinations of cyanates, thioesters, peroxides and heteroatom-halogen bonds.
liabilities: Aryl cyanates and formate/thioformate esters are chemically consequential reactive or hydrolyzable handles, not interchangeable benign decorations. Their stability and synthesis have not been demonstrated.

Late products combine heavy halogenation, multiple carbonyl derivatives and sulfur-containing chains; some contain S-F or O-O connections. Reduced average size still leaves a substantial oversized tail.

The dominant family is highly aromatic and mostly flat; alternative seeds add substantial conformational or topological complexity. Neither drawing style nor RDKit sanitization establishes a practical synthesis.
missing_features: The connected heteroaromatic acceptor arrangement is absent from the low-scoring fragments; abundant heteroatoms alone do not recreate it.

The listed high scorers offer little evidence of a substantially different core that retains the favorable arrangement while replacing the cyanate/formate/thioformate decorations with less reactive chemistry. Their equal scores do not reveal an exact missing decoration or required target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy/cyano polyaryl carbonyl compound scores 0.5418375031378128, whereas the thioaryl-linked, cyano-rich fused family reaches 0.6329826640983849. Tiny C=NOC, FF and other fragments remain at 0.5, showing that this floor is not evidence for useful molecular chemistry. The upper observed quartile has a median of 33 heavy atoms; late larger decorated heterocycles score around 0.595-0.597. The visible gradient therefore associates better scores with an intact acceptor-rich aromatic arrangement, without demonstrating a benefit from repeated appendage growth. Four different cyanate/formate/thioformate/acetate examples have exactly 0.6329826640983849, so their extra chemical liabilities are not distinguished by those values. The best cyano-rich seed rises from its Parent endpoint 0.6199818405862896, but the other Child seed endpoints, 0.5981257463267743 and 0.5965492580010727, are below their corresponding Parent values 0.6092799188640974 and 0.616992140985949.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring products are aryl-rich amines of moderate size, not nitrogen-poor fragments. The leader at 0.9999991193494832 has 29 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings, a tertiary piperidine, a secondary amine linker, a benzocyclobutene unit, an aryl thiol and carbon-bound fluorine and chlorine. Another leading family contains a bridged diazabicycle, two aryl groups, phenol, methoxy and aminomethyl substituents. These contain recognizable medicinal-chemistry building blocks, although the compact bridged arrangements are more demanding. The overall median is 30 heavy atoms versus 31 for the Parent; digest halogen_rate is 0.992. Late seed-2 output also contains N-chloro/N-bromo derivatives and tiny ClCl or CN(Cl)Cl. N-halogen-containing proposals increase from 82 in the Parent to 223 in the Child. Amine chemistry is already abundant; introducing a basic ring nitrogen cannot be described as a missing general capability here.
liabilities: The leading piperidine/benzocyclobutene molecule has three RDKit-detected unassigned atom stereocentres; the bridged phenol/aminomethyl leader has four. Apparent geometry and stereochemistry need more support than a connectivity-only score.

Aryl thiols and late N-Cl/N-Br groups introduce reactivity concerns. The stream includes both ordinary aryl halides and chemically distinct nitrogen-halogen bonds; they should not be treated as the same kind of fluorination or chlorination.
The benzocyclobutene and cage-like aza ring systems may be synthetically accessible in suitable cases, but no route or conformational feasibility evidence is supplied for these particular products.
missing_features: The low tail lacks the connected aromatic/nonacylated-amine combination present in the high scorers, or masks nitrogen with carbonyl/sulfonyl groups. The high scorers already supply this chemistry, so no additional necessary basic centre is established.

The high-scoring connectivities lack specified configurations and explicitly explored protonation states. Their neutral SMILES can still encode protonatable amines; the records do not show which charge state or stereoisomer would be favored.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low-scoring sulfonyl/disulfide fragment scores 0.00024675866379847753, and a carboxylic-acid, amide and N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine product scores 0.0006269216484658979. In contrast, every molecule in the upper observed quartile has an ordinary nonacylated amine structural flag, two aromatic rings and 23-32 heavy atoms. This supports a local preference for connected aryl/amine architecture and accessible amine functionality rather than larger, heavily acylated or sulfonylated assemblies. The nearly saturated scores do not establish a unique linker, thiol requirement, preferred stereoisomer or measured binding affinity. Parent best values 0.9959491085611949 and 0.9964552366323939 become 0.9999951970568197 and 0.9999991193494832 in seeds 0 and 1, while seed 2 changes from 0.9912887882944748 to 0.9697141867217297. The more reactive late amine substitutions do not provide a consistent improvement over the simpler leaders.

per_task.generated_character: Products are nitrogen-rich cyclic amides attached to aromatic groups, with a median of 34 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 56.6. One leading family carries a nine-membered triaza ring with two amide carbonyls, N-methyl substituents and two aryl groups, including an ethoxy-substituted aryl. The best molecule, 0.23402322695167738, has 29 heavy atoms and adds a short oxygen bridge across one arene; the phenol-bearing congener at 0.2338090388900024 has 31 heavy atoms and avoids that bridge. Another leading family, at 0.2339383623102592, has 35 heavy atoms and a fused/bridged nitrogen-rich aromatic framework joined to lactam and amine rings. Late products add further N-N or N-O connections. Compared with the Parent's median of 33 heavy atoms, size changes little, but mean perceived aromatic-ring count increases from 2.1528735632183906 to 2.7333333333333334. The ordinary amides and ethers are plausible fragments; the unusual short bridges and dense polycycles make whole-molecule synthesis much less certain.
liabilities: The short arene oxygen bridge is not an ordinary benzofuran motif. It creates a small constrained cycle whose geometric and synthetic feasibility cannot be inferred from sanitization.
Medium-sized cyclic diamides and densely fused aza/lactam systems can demand difficult cyclizations and stereochemical control; the leading examples leave their detected atom stereocentre unassigned.

Late N-O and additional N-N closures alter chemical roles as well as connectivity. Their presence should be evaluated individually; an N-O bond alone is not proof of instability, but these particular ring assemblies lack route evidence.
missing_features: The low fragments lack connected amide, amine and aromatic features; the favorable families preserve those roles but do not establish a specific missing ring, substitution position or external reference structure.

The supplied leaders do not consistently preserve a simple feasible topology while varying the relative placement of those functional groups. A phenol-bearing example already scores nearly as highly as the short oxygen-bridged structure, leaving no visible requirement for that additional bridge.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused carbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329, while the cyclic diamide/aryl and bridged lactam/aryl families approach 0.234. Methane, HCN and NOCl are at 0.0. All molecules in the upper observed quartile have an amide-type carbonyl/nitrogen connection and 29-40 heavy atoms, supporting retention of a connected nitrogen/carbonyl/aromatic arrangement. The arene oxygen bridge at 0.23402322695167738, the unbridged phenol family at 0.2338090388900024 and the more fused family at 0.2339383623102592 have very similar scores; extra ring complexity is therefore not evidence of a chemically meaningful gain. Parent seed-1's recorded best is 0.24321515648721753, above the corresponding Child value, while seeds 0 and 2 move from 0.22270606177144964 and 0.23035161967494103 to 0.2229315869550826 and 0.2339383623102592. Increased aromatic complexity is not uniformly associated with a better endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by fluorinated carbonyl/imino nitrogen heterocycles, usually retaining a fused aromatic core, with a median of 28 heavy atoms and digest mean SMILES length 53.3. The best molecule at 0.5387819611321613 has 29 heavy atoms: an N-fluorinated imino/lactam core, a fluorinated thiol-containing alkene chain, a substituted cyclobutene and an ester ending in another thiol. Other leaders have phenolic aryl groups, a partially unsaturated nitrogen ring, or a ring-expanded carbonyl-rich heterocycle with aminophenyl and pyrrolyl substituents. These are chemically more unusual than their moderate size alone suggests. Relative to the Parent, proposals with a perceived ring of at most four atoms increase from 91 to 378, and O-halogen-containing molecules from 77 to 231. N-halogen-containing molecules decrease from 534 to 279, so the change shifts liabilities rather than removing them. The leading cyclobutene/thiol structure has three unassigned atom stereocentres.
liabilities: Most leading fused examples contain N-F; the seed-0 leader additionally contains a C(=O)-O-Cl group. These bonds have different reactivity implications from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine and are not validated by a favorable score.

Fluorinated substituted cyclobutenes, unsaturated sulfur rings, multiple thiols and ester handles make stability and synthesis questionable. The increased small-ring frequency is an observed topological change, not proof of useful three-dimensional shape.

Atom configurations and alkene geometry are unspecified in the fluorinated sidechains and small rings. The top examples do not establish which realizable stereoisomer the recorded connectivity represents.
missing_features: The low and oversized products do not consistently preserve the compact carbonyl/nitrogen scaffold and positioned carbon-bound fluorine associated with the higher scores. More heterocycles or more fluorine atoms alone do not establish the same arrangement.

Many favorable structures lack a comparably supported combination of that arrangement with ordinary stable heteroatom bonding and specified stereochemistry. The trajectories do not identify a further required amine, stereoisomer or target-specific scaffold, and they do not show that N-F, O-Cl or a strained small ring is necessary.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A large repeated heteroaromatic/carbonyl assembly with 53 heavy atoms scores 1.5125441317900776e-37; a 47-heavy-atom indole/carbonyl assembly scores 7.32209661742749e-28. Compact fluorinated families instead reach roughly 0.5, whereas elemental fragments remain extremely poor. The most informative local comparison is the leader's fluorinated thiol sidechain at 0.5387819611321613 versus the otherwise corresponding late sidechain without that carbon-bound fluorine at 0.36175063935602336. This supports a position-sensitive fluorination association within this family, not a general rule that any fluorine bond helps. Replacing the terminal thiol of either the sidechain or ester appendage with fluorine gives the two listed examples at 0.5202350897378943. A ring-expanded example without N-F still reaches 0.5260004789707542, so N-F is not established as necessary across the observed chemistry. Parent endpoints 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.6025252354500499 become 0.5079089834520303, 0.5329941377390867 and 0.5387819611321613; the greater prevalence of small rings does not track a uniform score gain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Favorable structures coexist with electrophilic N-halogen and O-halogen links. For example, CN(c1ccc(F)c2c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n(C)c12)C1C(F)C=C(C(=O)OCl)SN1F scores 0.5079089834520303 and contains both N-F and acyl O-Cl. COc1c(C)c(OCF)cc2c1cc(C(=NF)Nc1ccccc1)n2Cl scores 0.3785808023129121 and places halogens directly on nitrogen. Elsewhere, the highest listed aryl/piperidine/secondary-amine molecule has ordinary nonacylated amine connections without N-halogen substitution. The output therefore shows access to conventional functionality, but no consistent preservation of it as graphs change; favorable scores alone do not certify these reactive bond types.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve ordinary heteroatom bonding while retaining useful polar functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: General chemical transformations should make it possible to preserve donor/acceptor roles and connected shape while changing reactive heteroatom substitutions into chemically coherent alternatives. Bond-level chemical context must distinguish ordinary carbon-bound halogens from nitrogen- or oxygen-bound halogens. This is a general stability and accessibility gap; it supplies neither a preferred scaffold nor an assumed objective reward for any replacement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: CCOc1ccccc1N1CCN(C)C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C1c1ccc2cc1O2 includes a short oxygen bridge across an arene and scores 0.23402322695167738. The phenol-bearing CCOc1ccc(CC)cc1N1CCN(C)C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C1c1ccccc1O scores 0.2338090388900024 without that bridge. C=Cc1cc2c3cc(C(=N)N(O)c4ccccc4)n2COc1c3C adds another constrained aromatic bridge at 0.4451945621839941. The fluorinated cyclobutene/thiol leader supplies a different small-ring liability. The digest's high ring_closure_rate documents abundant ring generation, so the missing capability is feasibility and controlled topology, not creating rings at all.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates ring closures without demonstrating that the resulting geometry is chemically realizable or useful.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring modification needs chemically informed closure, opening and simplification options that retain connected functional groups while respecting ring geometry and unsaturation. Assess particular bridges and strained-looking arrangements rather than banning every small or medium ring. The observed near-equal values provide no basis for assuming extra closures are inherently beneficial, and no particular ring size is prescribed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0. The listed leader CC(CCN1CCCCC1CNC1Cc2cc(Cl)ccc21)c1ccc(F)cc1S has three RDKit-detected unassigned atom stereocentres, and COc1cc(O)cc(CC2c3cc(F)ccc3C34CCC(CN3)N2C4)c1CN has four. Cn1c(=N)n(F)c(=O)c2c(C=CC(F)S)n(C3C=CC3(F)C(=O)OCS)c(F)c21 has three, together with unspecified sidechain alkene geometry. These are actual recorded high-scoring connectivities; the records supply no preferred stereochemical assignments.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical choices unspecified even when its products contain multiple apparent stereogenic features.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve stereochemical information when present and provide consistent, realizable configuration choices when edits create or alter stereogenic atoms or double bonds. Molecular identity should retain those distinctions. The need is to represent the chemical alternatives coherently; usefulness of any isomer must come from available feedback rather than an assumed target answer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes late O and FSSF at 0.0, C=NOC and FF at 0.5, and ClCl at 0.007765472974341367. At the opposite size extreme, CCOC(=O)c1ccc(O)c(-n2cc3c(c2C(=O)C2=CC=C(O)C(n4c5c6c(c4c4c5c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n4C)C=CC6)=CC2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3C)c1 has 53 heavy atoms and scores 1.5125441317900776e-37. The same supplied streams contain compact connected leaders with recognizable aromatic, amine or carbonyl roles. Another stream still contains 142 proposals above 50 heavy atoms despite a reduction in its mean size. Tiny fragmentation and redundant molecular growth therefore persist alongside useful bounded molecular families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Structural variation does not consistently maintain a coherent molecular scale and connected set of useful functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make structural variation capable of retaining connected functional roles while changing core connectivity or substituent placement, and provide ways to simplify repeated appendages. General chemical coherence and observed feedback should guide which scale works. The evidence does not justify a universal molecular-weight cutoff, fixed formula, task-specific size target or preferred fragment library.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
